explanation: Maintain the already reversed prefix and detach one node at a time from the remaining suffix, pointing it back to the prefix.
correctness: The prefix always contains the original first nodes in reverse order, and the suffix is untouched. Moving its first node extends the invariant until no suffix remains.
walkthrough: For nodes 3 -> 8 -> 1, first set node 3.Next to null. Next point the original node 8 to node 3, then point the original node 1 to node 8. Return the original node holding 1. The resulting values are [1,8,3], with every payload still attached to its original object. The callable returns the new head of the same node objects. JSON displays the returned head’s value sequence; the adapter also checks original identities, payloads and reversed links.
edgeCases: Empty input returns null; a singleton returns the same object. The old head becomes the tail with Next=null, even when payload values repeat.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: each of n nodes has its Next link rewritten once.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: current, saved next and previous references; no replacement nodes.
